prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right choice depends on your exact location, system type, urgency, budget and warranty. I can recommend well-reviewed local contractors if you tell me your Phoenix ZIP code or neighborhood. Meanwhile, here’s a quick, practical plan and what to look for when choosing a contractor.

If you want me to find nearby companies: tell me your ZIP code and whether this is an emergency (no cooling at all / high temp / after hours).

How to pick a good Phoenix HVAC contractor
- Licensing and insurance: confirm an Arizona ROC license number and liability insurance. Ask for the license number and verify it on the Arizona Registrar of Contractors website.  
- Certifications and training: look for NATE-certified technicians and manufacturer authorization for your system brand.  
- Local reputation: check recent Google/Yelp reviews, BBB rating and recent complaints. Prefer companies with many recent positive reviews.  
- Transparent pricing: get a written estimate that separates parts, labor, diagnostic fee and permits.  
- Warranties: ask about parts and labor warranty (and any manufacturer warranty transfer if replacing a unit).  
- Response time and emergency service: if it’s very hot and there’s no cooling, choose a company that offers same-day or emergency service.  
- Experience with your system: especially for older or high-efficiency systems, pick a contractor familiar with your brand and model.  
- Get multiple quotes: get at least 2–3 estimates for any major repair or replacement.

Questions to ask a contractor when you call
- Are you licensed with the Arizona Registrar of Contractors? What’s your license number?  
- Are your technicians NATE-certified?  
- Do you charge a diagnostic fee? (If yes, how much?)  
- What warranty do you provide on parts and labor?  
- Do you offer financing or same-day service?  
- Can you provide recent local references or reviews?

Quick troubleshooting steps you can try right now
- Thermostat: confirm it’s on COOL, batteries good, set lower than room temp.  
- Air filter: check/replace if dirty.  
- Circuit breaker: check the AC breaker and the outdoor unit disconnect switch.  
- Outdoor unit: make sure it’s free of debris and the fan is running.  
- Condensate drain: a clogged drain can trip float switches; look for water near the indoor unit.  
- Listen for unusual noises; note any error codes on the thermostat or indoor unit.

Typical costs (approximate)
- Service/diagnostic call: $75–$150.  
- Minor repairs (capacitor, contactor, sensors): $150–$700.  
- Major repairs (compressor, coil): $1,000–$3,000 — sometimes close to replacement cost for older systems.  
- New central AC replacement (installed): roughly $3,500–$8,000+, depending on size and efficiency.

If you want I can now:
- look up top-rated HVAC companies near you (provide ZIP), or  
- give a short list of well-reviewed Phoenix-area contractors and links to their reviews and license checks.

Which would you prefer?
